This is a small 57-residue cysteine-rich protein with eight cysteines, suggesting a defensin-like fold or toxin. I'm examining the sequence and cysteine spacing pattern, trying to match it against known toxin families like the CRISP-type or knottin scaffolds.

I'm now going through the CA coordinates residue by residue to trace the backbone geometry and infer secondary structure from distances.

I'm checking the i,i+3 spacing across this stretch of residues and most distances are coming out around 7-10, too large for tight helix, suggesting this segment is extended or loosely turned rather than a regular alpha helix.

Continuing the distance calculation gives another extended value, confirming most of the chain is in beta conformation rather than helical, punctuated by turns. Checking whether distant strands pair up doesn't show a clear match, so this looks like a predominantly beta-sheet structure.

I'll go with predominantly beta sheet as my final answer, matching the expected category format.
